I am a platform and systems engineer working at the intersection of infrastructure, security, and product. Most of my work is about making complex systems understandable, operable, and boring in the best possible way.
I spend my time designing and running cloud platforms and networks, and automation system, usually in regulated or high consequence environments. I care deeply about first principles, explicit constraints, and understanding how systems fail, not just how they work when everything is green.
This blog is where I write to think. I will be writing mostly technical notes, and whatever doesn’t fit elsewhere.
If you are interested in infrastructure, distributed systems, cloud platforms, or the uncomfortable edges where tools, incentives, and humans meet, I hope you will feel at home here.

data.building-dynamic-configuration-into-terr:
USENIX SREcon EMEA 2022 Infrastructure as Code Platform Engineering Amsterdam, NL • October 2022
Exposing opinionated entry points that let developers and managers update infrastructure and services without direct access to Terraform code or repositories is easier than ever with feature flags.
This talk explores the real challenges of running Terraform at scale, and how we reduced operational friction by separating configuration inputs from implementation. We’ll walk through the approach we used to move selected Terraform variables into a controlled external interface, allowing platform engineers to make targeted changes without triggering a full release or apply cycle.
Key takeaways:
Using feature flags we can expose inputs for Terraform. Reduce release coupling. Decouple low-risk operational changes from full plan apply cycles. Platform teams own the terraform, developers/managers own the inputs based on the enterprise Feature Management’s approval flows. Resources:
